_comment: SYNTHETIC cia-parity match-key vectors — single source of truth for both the offline TestMatchKeyCIAParity pin and the env-gated DS_CIA_PARITY drift check. Each vector's `key` is the cia-byte-compatible match key, derived directly from the REAL cia.cassette library (match_key(normalize_request(...))) — NOT a Go echo. The offline TestMatchKeyCIAParity pins them so a regression in the Go port fails loudly with no live cia; the env-gated DS_CIA_PARITY=1 manual run re-derives the same keys against the local cia checkout (deferred manual step, never CI). A passing offline test plus a passing manual run together prove byte-for-byte cross-tool match-key parity, so a cassette recorded by either tool replays through the other. method/path are POST /v1/messages for every vector. The three encoder hazards a naive json.Marshal diverges on are deliberately exercised: non-ASCII (ensure_ascii \uXXXX), the <>& chars (Go HTML-escapes, Python does not), and a multi-turn growing-history body. The widened vectors target CAPTURE-TOOL-DESIGN.md §7's most-likely-subtle-bug surface at zero live-run cost: varied image media_type (note media_type is NOT part of the key — only source.data is hashed, so a media_type change must NOT move the key), multi-image content blocks, and mixed tool_result+text content (including a tool_result whose content is itself a block list). The block-shape vectors (document/PDF source, cache_control marker, thinking, redacted_thinking) close the CAPTURE-TOOL-DESIGN.md §6 Q3 / §7 gap: cia's _content_text routes document/thinking/redacted_thinking through its else-branch (btype + ':' + json.dumps(block, sort_keys=True, default=str) — DEFAULT separators ', '/': ', ensure_ascii, NO HTML escaping), so the entire block is folded into the key; cache_control is a MARKER on a known block and is DROPPED (the text branch keys only block.get('text')), so toggling it must NOT move the key. The document-nonascii-htmlchars vector pins the else-branch encoder against the same ensure_ascii / no-HTML-escape hazards but NESTED inside a sub-encoded block. SYNTHETIC ONLY (D50): fake model id claude-synthetic-test-1, no real model text, no creds, no real paths/costs/tokens/Bearer.

vectors.name: html-chars-no-escape

messages.content: if a < b && c > d then <tag>

vectors.key: claude-synthetic-test-1|turns=1|if a < b && c > d then <tag>|fdfa84a6073b6ffb

vectors.name: document-pdf-source
vectors._note: Anthropic `document` content block with a base64 PDF source. cia has no special case for `document`, so it falls to _content_text's else-branch: `document:` + json.dumps(whole_block, sort_keys=True, default=str) with Python DEFAULT separators (', '/': '). The whole block — source.{type,media_type,data} — is folded into the key (unlike `image`, which hashes only source.data). cia-truth key derived from cia.cassette.match_key(normalize_request(...)).

vectors.name: document-nonascii-htmlchars
vectors._note: A `document` block carrying non-ASCII (ÿœö ☃ résumé) and the <>& chars in a title field, to pin the else-branch json.dumps NESTED encoder against the two byte-compat hazards: non-ASCII MUST become \uXXXX (ensure_ascii) and <>& MUST stay raw (Python does not HTML-escape; Go's default encoder would). This is the document/PDF analogue of the top-level html-chars-no-escape + non-ascii-ensure-ascii vectors, but inside a sub-encoded block. cia-truth key from cia.cassette.

vectors.name: cache-control-on-text
vectors._note: cache_control is a MARKER on a known `text` block. cia's _content_text text-branch keys ONLY block.get('text') — cache_control is dropped — so this keys identically to two plain text blocks (`text:cached preamble` + `text:live question`). Toggling/removing cache_control must NOT move the key; this vector pins that drop. cia-truth key from cia.cassette.

vectors.name: cache-control-on-system
vectors._note: cache_control marker on a list-form system prompt. system goes through _content_text, so the text-branch again drops cache_control and keys only `text:You are a test fixture.`. Pins that a cached system block keys the same as the uncached one. cia-truth key from cia.cassette.

vectors.name: thinking-block
vectors._note: Extended-thinking `thinking` block (thinking text + signature) in an assistant turn. cia has no special case, so the else-branch folds the WHOLE block via `thinking:` + json.dumps(block, sort_keys=True, default=str) (default separators) — both the thinking text and the signature participate in the key. cia-truth key from cia.cassette.

content.thinking: Let me reason step by step about the problem.

vectors.name: redacted-thinking-block
vectors._note: `redacted_thinking` block (opaque `data` blob) in an assistant turn. Else-branch again: `redacted_thinking:` + json.dumps(block, sort_keys=True, default=str). The opaque data blob participates in the key. cia-truth key from cia.cassette.
